newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber extends fall at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber extends fall at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended losses at the close as the market moved in tandem with a weaker Tokyo market, dealers said.
They said lack of demand from overseas buyers also weighed on prices.
"It's a very quiet market. With no new factors in the market, Tokyo provided the only lead," said one dealer.
Japanese rubber futures fell across the board, depressed by near-term oversupply trends.
Dealers said prices were likely to continue their drift unless demand picks up.
There was still no sign of European buyers returning to the market after the summer holidays, they said.

At the close, benchmark October RSS1 buyer was quoted at 317.50 cents ($1.27) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down 2.50 cents from Tuesday. October SMR20 buyer was down a cent at 309.50 cents ($1.24) a kg.
Prices offered by trading houses were slightly lower from the morning. SMR CV was offered at 372 cents, SMR L at 352, SMR 5 at 322, SMR 10 at 310.50 and drum latex at 240-242.
